newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Redrow never been in better shape.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Redrow never been in better shape.

text.p: Steve Morgan, chairman of Redrow Group Plc, said on Tuesday he was selling 54 million shares in the construction company at a time when the group was in a better shape than ever before.

The sale will bring Morgan's holding down to 35 percent from 59 percent. Morgan told Reuters he did not intend selling more shares. "I still have a very meaningful holding in this business and I am fully committed to it," he said.
Morgan added he originally wanted to reduce his stake to a minority holding three years ago when Redrow was floated.
But a weak market at the time made him postpone the sale, which Morgan considered necessary to ensure Redrow would be perceived as true public company.
But times have changed as the housing market picked up and appears to be growing at sustainable rates, prompting Morgan to sell now.
"The company is in superb shape; it has a strong orderbook, strong landbank, 23 percent plus return on capital and the market looks set to continue," Morgan said.
Redrow earlier reported a profit rise to 16.4 million stg in the six months to December 31 from 12.1 million a year earlier. Turnover rose by 29 percent to 123.2 million stg.
Morgan said the housing market this time around lacked the gung-ho feeling which helped prices rocket ahead in the late 1980s only to see them fall down like bricks again soon after.
In contrast, the market now seems to keep both feet firmly on the ground, suggesting that the current upturn is sustainable, Morgan said.
"It has a much more permanent feel about it with inflation in single figures," said Morgan. "People are dismissing the election and get on with their lifes," he added.
The share sale, through a book-building procedure, is scheduled to be completed towards the end of next week.
